survey: Image 5 is a gold five-pointed sheriff's star badge, seen roughly face-on and floating against a purple sunburst background. Its parts: a bevelled star body with a ridge running down the middle of each arm; a ball finial on the tip of each of the five points; and a round raised boss in the centre holding a red domed gem. The ball finials sit right on the tips and look attached, and the centre boss is set into the body. The back, where a pin would go, can't be seen, and that's fine for a front view. A badge doesn't need to rest on anything, so floating is acceptable here. Every ball finial is shown about the same size, so the view is close to frontal and tilt doesn't explain the arm lengths differing.

errors.where: Star body, all five arms (most visible in the short lower-left arm compared with the long top and right arms)
errors.what: The star is lopsided. A real five-point badge is stamped from a regular shape, but here the arms differ in length and width and the inner notches sit at uneven depths and angles. The lower-left arm is clearly stubby next to the others. Because the view is nearly frontal, this is a shape fault, not foreshortening.
There's an invented part: a glossy red jewel in the centre boss. Real sheriff's badges have a flat or engraved round seal in the centre, not a gemstone.

fix: Gold sheriff's star badge, a regular five-pointed star with all five arms equal in length and width and evenly spaced inner notches, a ball finial on each tip, and a flat engraved round gold seal in the centre instead of a red gem.
